data.title: Descriptions
data.tagline: Show the field names and values of one record
data.description: A description list pairs labels with read-only values for an order, account, or project. It may look similar to a form, but its main job is viewing. When people need to change the information, move them into a clearly editable form.

avoid: Use editable controls without an editing state
Show dozens of fields with no grouping
Let long values break the label-value relationship
Use it to compare many records; use a Table

lessonPractice.title: An order detail page shows eight read-only fields such as recipient, amount, and status, with no editing here. How should it be organized?

options.label: Use label-and-value descriptions and adjust the number of columns for available width
options.feedback: These are read-only properties of one record, so paired labels and values make them easy to verify.

options.label: Put all eight values in disabled inputs to preserve the appearance of an edit page
options.feedback: Disabled controls imply potential editing and add visual noise when the task only requires reading.

options.label: Create an eight-column table with the single order in one row
options.feedback: Tables suit comparing many records by column. One row across eight columns compresses badly on narrow screens.

data.agentPrompt: Present read-only order details as label-and-value descriptions rather than disabled inputs. Allow columns on desktop and switch to one column on mobile; test alignment and wrapping with long addresses, empty values, and long status text.
